questions.q: Which part of tragedy does Aristotle call its "soul"?
questions.explain: Plot, the arrangement of the incidents, comes first. Character comes second.

questions.q: A messenger arrives to comfort the hero and, by doing so, reveals the truth that destroys him. This is a…
questions.explain: An action producing the opposite of its intended effect is a reversal. Aristotle's example is the messenger in Oedipus.

questions.q: What does Aristotle consider the worst kind of plot?
choices: Episodic: events with no probable or necessary link
Short: under a day in length
questions.explain: Episodic plots string events together without cause. That's "after" rather than "because of".

questions.q: Which of the "three unities" did Aristotle actually insist on?
questions.explain: Only unity of action. Time was an observation, place he never mentions; the three unities came from later Renaissance and neoclassical critics.

questions.q: A real event in your script is true but the audience finds it unbelievable. Which Aristotelian principle applies?
choices: Prefer probable impossibilities to improbable possibilities
Plot is the soul of tragedy
A whole has a beginning, middle and end
questions.explain: What matters on stage is whether it feels probable, not whether it could really happen.
It means an error, often made in ignorance. It isn't necessarily a defect of character.

questions.q: Aristotle criticizes Euripides' Medea for its ending. Why?
choices: It resolves through a deus ex machina, not the plot itself
questions.explain: The unraveling should come out of the plot, not from outside intervention.

questions.q: Who called Aristotle's model of tragedy a "coercive system"?
questions.explain: Augusto Boal, in Theatre of the Oppressed (1974).

ideas: Plot is the soul of drama; character comes second.
The best turning point combines a reversal of fortune with a recognition, a shift from ignorance to knowledge.
An audience prefers a probable impossibility to an improbable possibility.
A drama should imitate one unified action, not everything that happens to one hero.
